claim: In the lesioned zebrafish retina, Müller glia produce multipotent retinal progenitors that generate all retinal neurons, replacing lost cell types.
source: In the lesioned zebrafish retina, Müller glia produce multipotent retinal progenitors that generate all retinal neurons, replacing lost cell types.
evidence: This is a summary statement from the abstract that synthesizes the overall finding of the study.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to study Müller glia, progenitors and regenerated progeny from uninjured and light-lesioned retinae.
source: To study the molecular mechanisms linking Müller glia reactivity to progenitor production and neuronal differentiation, we used single-cell RNA sequencing of Müller glia, progenitors and regenerated progeny from uninjured and light-lesioned retinae.
evidence: The methodology is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: An injury-induced Müller glia differentiation trajectory leads into a cell population with a hybrid identity expressing marker genes of Müller glia and progenitors.
source: We discover an injury-induced Müller glia differentiation trajectory that leads into a cell population with a hybrid identity expressing marker genes of Müller glia and progenitors.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the abstract as a key discovery.

claim: A glial self-renewal trajectory departs from the hybrid cell population.
source: A glial self-renewal and a neurogenic trajectory depart from the hybrid cell population.
evidence: This trajectory is explicitly described in the abstract.

claim: A neurogenic trajectory departs from the hybrid cell population.
source: A glial self-renewal and a neurogenic trajectory depart from the hybrid cell population.
evidence: This trajectory is explicitly described in the abstract.

claim: Neurogenic progenitors progressively differentiate to generate retinal ganglion cells first and bipolar cells last, similar to events observed during retinal development.
source: We further observe that neurogenic progenitors progressively differentiate to generate retinal ganglion cells first and bipolar cells last, similar to the events observed during retinal development.
evidence: This temporal sequence of differentiation is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: The vertebrate retina is the neural tissue in the back of the eyes that detects and processes visual stimuli prior to transmission to the brain.
source: The vertebrate retina is the neural tissue in the back of the eyes that detects and processes visual stimuli prior to transmission to the brain (Dowling, 1987).
evidence: This is a cited statement of established knowledge about retinal function.

claim: The retina has a layered structure with outer, inner and ganglion cell nuclear layers alternating with the outer and inner plexiform layers.
source: The retina has a layered structure, with outer, inner and ganglion cell nuclear layers alternating with the outer and inner plexiform layers (Amini et al., 2017; Hoon et al., 2014; Stenkamp, 2015).
evidence: This anatomical description is supported by multiple citations.

claim: There are six distinct classes of retinal neurons and one main type of glia: retinal ganglion, cone photoreceptor, horizontal, amacrine, rod photoreceptor and bipolar cells, as well as Müller glia.
source: There are six distinct classes of retinal neurons and one main type of glia: retinal ganglion, cone photoreceptor, horizontal, amacrine, rod photoreceptor and bipolar cells, as well as Müller glia.
evidence: This classification of retinal cell types is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Retinal cell heterogeneity arises during development in the indicated order from a common pool of multipotent retinal progenitor cells, which progressively restrict their competence to generate early and mid-late born cell fates.
source: This heterogeneity arises during development in the indicated order from a common pool of multipotent retinal progenitor cells (RPCs), which progressively restrict their competence to generate early and mid-late born cell fates (Agathocleous and Harris, 2009; Alexiades and Cepko, 1997; Amini et al., 2017; Cepko, 2014; Cepko et al., 1996; Livesey and Cepko, 2001; Stenkamp, 2015; Stenkamp, 2007; Turner and Cepko, 1987; Weber et al., 2014; Young, 1985).
evidence: This developmental principle is supported by extensive citations.

claim: Retinal development, structure and function are highly conserved among vertebrates, including the teleost zebrafish (Danio rerio) with some variations.
source: Retinal development, structure and function are highly conserved among vertebrates, including the teleost zebrafish (Danio rerio) with some variations.
evidence: This statement of evolutionary conservation is presented as established knowledge.

claim: Humans and zebrafish possess a cone-dominated retina adapted for diurnal visual tasks, whereas nocturnal animals, like mice and rats, have rod-dominated retinae adapted for a dim light lifestyle.
source: For instance, humans and zebrafish possess a cone-dominated retina adapted for diurnal visual tasks, whereas nocturnal animals, like mice and rats, have rod-dominated retinae adapted for a dim light lifestyle (Fleisch et al., 2011; Saade et al., 2013; Stenkamp, 2007).
evidence: This comparative statement about retinal composition is supported by citations.

claim: Adult zebrafish can fully regenerate their retinae upon lesions affecting different neuronal cell types, in contrast to warm-blooded vertebrates like birds and mammals.
source: Intriguingly, and in contrast to warm-blooded vertebrates like birds and mammals, adult zebrafish can fully regenerate their retinae upon lesions affecting different neuronal cell types, depending on the injury paradigm.
evidence: This regenerative capacity is stated as a distinguishing feature of zebrafish.

claim: Intense light ablates preferentially light-sensing rod and cone photoreceptors in the central and dorsal retina.
source: For instance, intense light ablates preferentially light-sensing rod and cone photoreceptors in the central and dorsal retina, whereas application of neurotoxins, like ouabain or NMDA, affects mainly retinal ganglion and amacrine cells (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fimbel et al., 2007; Powell et al., 2016; Sherpa et al., 2008; Vihtelic et al., 2006; Vihtelic and Hyde, 2000; Weber et al., 2013).
evidence: This effect of light lesion is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Application of neurotoxins, like ouabain or NMDA, affects mainly retinal ganglion and amacrine cells.
source: For instance, intense light ablates preferentially light-sensing rod and cone photoreceptors in the central and dorsal retina, whereas application of neurotoxins, like ouabain or NMDA, affects mainly retinal ganglion and amacrine cells (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fimbel et al., 2007; Powell et al., 2016; Sherpa et al., 2008; Vihtelic et al., 2006; Vihtelic and Hyde, 2000; Weber et al., 2013).
evidence: This effect of neurotoxins is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Müller glia, acting as resident stem cells, are the primary cellular origin of regenerated cells, independently of the lesion type.
source: Independently of the lesion type, Müller glia (MG), acting as resident stem cells, are the primary cellular origin of regenerated cells.
evidence: This role of Müller glia is stated as a general principle.

claim: Zebrafish MG react to lesion by partial dedifferentiation that takes place between 6 and 24 hr post lesion.
source: Specifically, zebrafish MG react to the lesion by partial dedifferentiation that takes place between 6 and 24 hr post lesion, followed by cell cycle re-entry, including up-regulation of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), a marker of the S-G2/M cell cycle phases (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fausett et al., 2008; Nagashima et al., 2013; Raymond et al., 2006).
evidence: This temporal sequence is supported by citations.

claim: PCNA expression in MG is initiated at 24–31 hr post lesion.
source: PCNA expression in MG is initiated at 24–31 hr post lesion (Lahne et al., 2015; Nelson et al., 2013; Thummel et al., 2008) and can still be detected up to 2 days post lesion (Nagashima et al., 2013; Nelson et al., 2013).
evidence: This timing of PCNA expression is supported by citations.

claim: PCNA upregulation is followed by asymmetric cell division of the MG that produces renewed MG and multipotent RPCs, which are detected starting from 51 hr post lesion.
source: PCNA upregulation is followed by asymmetric cell division of the MG that produces renewed MG and multipotent RPCs, which are detected starting from 51 hr post lesion (Gorsuch and Hyde, 2014; Lahne et al., 2020a; Lenkowski and Raymond, 2014; Thummel et al., 2008; Wan and Goldman, 2016).
evidence: This sequence of events is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Dedifferentiation of MG to a progenitor-like state is not complete, as MG upregulate progenitor-associated genes like pax6 or vsx2, but retain their glial morphology.
source: Dedifferentiation of MG to a progenitor-like state is not complete, as MG upregulate progenitor-associated genes like pax6 or vsx2, but retain their glial morphology.
evidence: This incomplete dedifferentiation is stated as an observation.

claim: Glial markers like Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (gfap) as well as glutamine synthase (glula) have been reported to be either retained or downregulated, depending on the lesion paradigm, the regeneration time point, the antibody and the transgenic line used to label MG.
source: In this context, glial markers like Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (gfap) as well as glutamine synthase (glula) have been reported to be either retained or downregulated, depending on the lesion paradigm, the regeneration time point, the antibody and the transgenic line used to label MG (Fimbel et al., 2007; Lenkowski and Raymond, 2014; Nagashima et al., 2013; Thummel et al., 2008).
evidence: This variability in marker expression is supported by citations.

claim: In all reported cases, MG-derived RPCs do not express gfap.
source: However, in all reported cases, MG-derived RPCs do not express gfap (Lenkowski and Raymond, 2014; Thummel et al., 2008).
evidence: This consistent observation is supported by citations.

claim: Asymmetric cell division of MG occurs between 31 hr and 2 days post-lesion, followed by further proliferation of MG-derived RPCs that peaks at 4–5 days post lesion.
source: Asymmetric cell division of MG occurs between 31 hr and 2 days post-lesion, followed by further proliferation of MG-derived RPCs that peaks at 4–5 days post lesion, depending on the injury paradigm (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fausett and Goldman, 2006; Fimbel et al., 2007; Lahne et al., 2015; Nagashima et al., 2013; Nelson et al., 2013; Thummel et al., 2008).
evidence: This temporal sequence is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Studies on zebrafish retina regeneration have so far mainly focused on very early phases of MG dedifferentiation and RPC production.
source: Studies on zebrafish retina regeneration have so far mainly focused on very early phases of MG dedifferentiation and RPC production (Fausett et al., 2008; Nelson et al., 2013; Ramachandran et al., 2010; Ramachandran et al., 2011; Thummel et al., 2008; Thummel et al., 2010; Wan et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2014).
evidence: This characterization of prior research is supported by citations.

claim: MG initially assume a reactive state, characterized by the expression of hmga1a and yap1, prior to giving rise to proliferative, neurogenic RPCs.
source: Recent work showed that MG initially assume a reactive state, characterized by the expression of hmga1a and yap1, prior to giving rise to proliferative, neurogenic RPCs (Hoang et al., 2020).
evidence: This finding from recent work is supported by a citation.

claim: Impaired Yap1 or Hmga1a function impedes MG reprogramming and neurogenesis in the regenerating retina.
source: Consequently, impaired Yap1 or Hmga1a function impedes MG reprogramming and neurogenesis in the regenerating retina (Hoang et al., 2020).
evidence: This functional consequence is supported by a citation.

claim: The molecular and cellular identities of self-renewed MG and MG-derived RPCs remain elusive.
source: In contrast, the molecular and cellular identities of self-renewed MG and MG-derived RPCs remain elusive.
evidence: This gap in knowledge is explicitly stated.

claim: RPCs have fusiform nuclei that closely associate with GFAP-positive glial fibers across the inner nuclear layer.
source: RPCs have fusiform nuclei that closely associate with GFAP-positive glial fibers across the inner nuclear layer.
evidence: This morphological description is stated as an observation.

claim: RPCs express markers of multipotency, like Pax6 and Sox2, as well as markers of neurogenesis, like Atoh7.
source: They also express markers of multipotency, like Pax6 and Sox2, as well as markers of neurogenesis, like Atoh7 (Fausett and Goldman, 2006; Gorsuch et al., 2017; Nagashima et al., 2013; Raymond et al., 2006; Thummel et al., 2010).
evidence: This marker expression is supported by citations.

claim: Previous studies have investigated RPCs molecular identity mainly at the population level.
source: Previous studies have investigated RPCs molecular identity mainly at the population level (Cameron et al., 2005; Hoang et al., 2020; Kassen et al., 2007; Kramer et al., 2021; Lahne et al., 2020a; Morris et al., 2011; Ng Chi Kei et al., 2017; Powell et al., 2016; Qin et al., 2009; Ramachandran et al., 2012; Thummel et al., 2008).
evidence: This characterization of prior research is supported by citations.

claim: A detailed characterization of the transcriptional network underlying RPC production and RPC differentiation, as well as the lineage relationships between MG, RPCs and differentiating progeny is currently missing.
source: However, a detailed characterization of the transcriptional network underlying RPC production and RPC differentiation, as well as the lineage relationships between MG, RPCs and differentiating progeny is currently missing.
evidence: This gap in knowledge is explicitly stated.

claim: The study profiled the transcriptome of MG and MG-derived RPCs in response to an intense light lesion, and followed their differentiation trajectories towards regenerated retinal neurons at the single cell level.
source: Here, we profiled the transcriptome of MG and MG-derived RPCs in response to an intense light lesion, and followed their differentiation trajectories towards regenerated retinal neurons at the single cell level.
evidence: This describes the approach taken in the study.

claim: The study addressed the transcriptional state of reactive MG prior to and after their asymmetric cell division.
source: In particular, we addressed the transcriptional state of reactive MG prior to and after their asymmetric cell division.
evidence: This is stated as a specific aim of the study.

claim: The study addressed whether MG-derived RPCs are heterogeneous and to what extent they express molecular markers that are observed during embryonic retinogenesis.
source: Moreover, we addressed whether MG-derived RPCs are heterogeneous and to what extent they express molecular markers that are observed during embryonic retinogenesis (Xu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a specific aim of the study.

claim: A short-term lineage tracing strategy was employed that allowed the isolation of individual MG and MG-derived cells of the regenerating zebrafish retina, which were subsequently subjected to droplet-based, 10 x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq).
source: To this aim, we employed a short-term lineage tracing strategy that allowed the isolation of individual MG and MG-derived cells of the regenerating zebrafish retina, which were subsequently subjected to droplet-based, 10 x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: MG can be non-reactive in uninjured and lesioned conditions, as well as reactive upon lesion.
source: We find that MG can be non-reactive in uninjured and lesioned conditions, as well as reactive upon lesion.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Reactive MG give rise to a hybrid cell population, which replenishes the pool of MG as well as feeds into the pool of neurogenic RPCs.
source: Reactive MG give rise to a hybrid cell population, which replenishes the pool of MG as well as feeds into the pool of neurogenic RPCs.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: MG-derived RPCs are highly heterogeneous and display a progressive restriction in their competence during subsequent differentiation.
source: Moreover, MG-derived RPCs are highly heterogeneous and display a progressive restriction in their competence during subsequent differentiation.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: MG-derived RPCs upregulate developmental markers of retinogenesis and produce regenerated neurons partially according to the developmental birth order, with retinal ganglion cells born first and bipolar cells born last.
source: They upregulate developmental markers of retinogenesis and produce regenerated neurons partially according to the developmental birth order, with retinal ganglion cells born first and bipolar cells born last.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The pcna:EGFP transgene drives the expression of EGFP under the regulatory elements of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (pcna), a known marker of proliferating cells.
source: The former drives the expression of EGFP under the regulatory elements of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (pcna), a known marker of proliferating cells, and thereby labels actively dividing cells, and, due to the persistence of EGFP, their short-term progeny.
evidence: This describes the function of the transgenic reporter.

claim: The gfap:mCherry transgene drives expression of mCherry under the regulatory elements of glial fibrillary acidic protein (gfap), a known marker of zebrafish MG.
source: The other reporter drives expression of mCherry under the regulatory elements of glial fibrillary acidic protein (gfap), a known marker of zebrafish MG.
evidence: This describes the function of the transgenic reporter.

claim: Both transgenes recapitulate the endogenous expression in the adult zebrafish retina faithfully.
source: Both transgenes recapitulate the endogenous expression in the adult zebrafish retina faithfully (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This validation is stated and supported by reference to a figure.

claim: Immunohistochemistry against the proliferation marker PCNA co-labeled pcna:EGFP-positive cells mainly in the ciliary marginal zone.
source: Immunohistochemistry against the proliferation marker PCNA co-labeled pcna:EGFP-positive cells mainly in the ciliary marginal zone, one of the stem cells niches in the adult zebrafish retina (Bernardos et al., 2007; Raymond et al., 2006).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citations and figure reference.

claim: The MG-specific antibody Zrf1 labeled virtually all gfap:mCherry-positive cells in the central retina as well as in the ciliary marginal zone.
source: The MG-specific antibody Zrf1 labeled virtually all gfap:mCherry-positive cells in the central retina as well as in the ciliary marginal zone (Bernardos et al., 2007; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: At 44 hours post light lesion (hpl), MG are about to undergo or have already completed their asymmetric cell division giving rise to the first RPCs and self-renewed MG.
source: First, 44 hours post light lesion (hpl), when MG are about to undergo or have already completed their asymmetric cell division giving rise to the first RPCs and self-renewed MG (Lahne et al., 2015; Nagashima et al., 2013).
evidence: This timing is stated and supported by citations.

claim: 4 days post light lesion (dpl) represents the peak of RPC proliferation.
source: Second, 4 days post light lesion (dpl), representing the peak of RPC proliferation (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fausett and Goldman, 2006)
evidence: This timing is stated and supported by citations.

claim: At 6 dpl, the first differentiating, regenerated progeny arise.
source: and third, 6 dpl, when the first differentiating, regenerated progeny arise (Bernardos et al., 2007).
evidence: This timing is stated and supported by a citation.

claim: Uninjured, central retinae displayed no EGFP, but strong mCherry signal consistent with non-proliferating MG.
source: Uninjured, central retinae displayed no EGFP, but strong mCherry signal consistent with non-proliferating MG (white arrowheads).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Numerous EGFP/mCherry double-positive cells were present at 44 hpl, indicating potential cell-cycle re-entry of MG.
source: In contrast, numerous EGFP/mCherry double-positive cells were present at 44 hpl, indicating potential cell-cycle re-entry of MG (yellow arrowheads).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 4 dpl, overall mCherry expression was reduced, consistent with the previously described downregulation of the gfap promoter by MG-derived RPCs.
source: At 4 dpl, overall mCherry expression was reduced, consistent with the previously described downregulation of the gfap promoter by MG-derived RPCs (Fimbel et al., 2007; Lenkowski and Raymond, 2014; Thummel et al., 2008).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citations and figure reference.

claim: EGFP was strongly found throughout all retinal layers at 4 dpl, matching the reported peak in proliferation of MG-derived RPCs.
source: In contrast, EGFP was strongly found throughout all retinal layers, matching the reported peak in proliferation of MG-derived RPCs (red arrowheads) (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fausett and Goldman, 2006; Fimbel et al., 2007; Lenkowski and Raymond, 2014; Thummel et al., 2008).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citations and figure reference.

claim: An increase in mCherry accompanies a decline in EGFP signal at 6 dpl in comparison to 4 dpl.
source: Finally, in comparison to 4 dpl, an increase in mCherry accompanies a decline in EGFP signal at 6 dpl (yellow arrowhead).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Flow cytometry plots confirmed the rationale of the cell isolation strategy.
source: Flow cytometry plots confirmed the rationale of the above-mentioned strategy (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This validation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Non-fluorescent and EGFP-positive only cells were detected in all samples, consistent with non-proliferating and proliferating cells in the adult zebrafish retina.
source: In all samples, we detected non-fluorescent and EGFP-positive only cells, consistent with non-proliferating and proliferating cells in the adult zebrafish retina.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cell populations expressing only mCherry were detected at all sampled time points, most likely representing non-reactive MG.
source: We also detected cell populations expressing only mCherry at all sampled time points, most likely representing non-reactive MG.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: EGFP/mCherry-double positive cells were found in all samples consistent with proliferating MG originating from the ciliary marginal zone and the central retina.
source: In addition to cells expressing either EGFP or mCherry, we find EGFP/mCherry-double positive cells in all samples consistent with proliferating MG originating from the ciliary marginal zone and the central retina (see Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: The EGFP/mCherry-double positive population increased at 44 hpl, presumably due to an increase in the cell number of reactive, proliferating MG.
source: The EGFP/mCherry-double positive population increased at 44 hpl, presumably due to an increase in the cell number of reactive, proliferating MG.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: A second, EGFP-positive, lower mCherry-positive cell population was detected at 44 hpl, presumably including the very first RPCs resulting from MG cell division at this time point.
source: A second, EGFP-positive, lower mCherry-positive cell population was detected at 44 hpl, presumably including the very first RPCs resulting from MG cell division at this time point.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 4 dpl, the large EGFP/mCherry-double positive cell population was still present, but displayed a lower mCherry, yet an increased EGFP signal, in line with MG-derived RPCs, which exhibit maximal proliferation at 4 dpl.
source: At 4 dpl, the large EGFP/mCherry-double positive cell population was still present, but displayed a lower mCherry, yet an increased EGFP signal, in line with MG-derived RPCs, which exhibit maximal proliferation at 4 dpl (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fausett and Goldman, 2006).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citations and figure reference.

claim: At 6 dpl, a further decreased mCherry intensity was observed for the EGFP/mCherry-double positive cell population.
source: At 6 dpl, a further decreased mCherry intensity was observed for the EGFP/mCherry-double positive cell population.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: 15,000 cells per time point were sorted from retinae of uninjured, 44 hpl, 4 dpl, and 6 dpl samples.
source: In order to profile the transcriptome of individual MG, RPCs and progeny of the uninjured and light lesioned retinae, we dissected retinae of the before-mentioned time points (uninjured, 44 hpl, 4 dpl, 6 dpl) and eventually sorted 15,000 cells per time point.
evidence: This experimental detail is stated.

claim: A sorting gate that included both mCherry-positive only and EGFP/mCherry-double positive cells was applied at the sampled time points.
source: We applied a sorting gate that included both mCherry-positive only and EGFP/mCherry-double positive cells at the sampled time points (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This experimental detail is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Non-fluorescent as well as EGFP-only positive cells were not included in the sorting.
source: Non-fluorescent as well as EGFP- only positive cells were not included.
evidence: This experimental detail is stated.

claim: Sorted cells underwent 10 x Genomics scRNAseq and 13,139 cells passed the sequencing quality control.
source: Sorted cells underwent 10 x Genomics scRNAseq and 13,139 cells passed the sequencing quality control.
evidence: This experimental result is stated.

claim: A median of 1,407 genes and 4,061 mean read counts per cell were detected.
source: We detected a median of 1.407 genes and 4.061 mean read counts per cell.
evidence: This sequencing metric is stated.

claim: Three clusters were initially identified for the full dataset: a retinal core dataset and two additional clusters identified as microglia and ribosomal gene-enriched cells.
source: Initially, we identified three clusters for the full dataset (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A): a retinal core dataset and two additional clusters identified as microglia and ribosomal gene-enriched cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This clustering result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Microglia and ribosomal gene-enriched cell populations were excluded from the subsequent analysis.
source: Both populations were excluded from the subsequent analysis.
evidence: This analytical decision is stated.

claim: Re-clustering of the core dataset, which eventually included 11,690 cells, revealed 15 potential, different cell populations.
source: Re-clustering of the core dataset, which eventually included 11,690 cells, revealed 15 potential, different cell populations (Figure 2A).
evidence: This clustering result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: From left to right on the UMAP, the progressive emergence of MG, RPC and progeny clusters was observed.
source: From left to right on the UMAP, which visualizes the cell lineage trajectory, we observed the progressive emergence of MG, RPC and progeny clusters.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Four MG clusters (clusters 1–4) were identified that locate to the left and middle portion of the map.
source: In detail, we identified four MG clusters (clusters 1–4) that locate to the left and middle portion of the map, followed by five RPC clusters (clusters 5–9) locating to the right side of the map.
evidence: This cluster identification is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Five RPC clusters (clusters 5–9) were identified locating to the right side of the map.
source: In detail, we identified four MG clusters (clusters 1–4) that locate to the left and middle portion of the map, followed by five RPC clusters (clusters 5–9) locating to the right side of the map.
evidence: This cluster identification is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Regenerated progeny branch from the RPCs and include retinal ganglion (cluster 10), amacrine (cluster 13) and bipolar cells (cluster 15) at the bottom-right, as well as red and blue cones (clusters 11 and 12) at the top-right of the map.
source: Regenerated progeny branch from the RPCs and include retinal ganglion (cluster 10), amacrine (cluster 13) and bipolar cells (cluster 15) at the bottom-right, as well as red and blue cones (clusters 11 and 12) at the top-right of the map.
evidence: This cluster identification is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: There is a second cluster of amacrine cells (cluster 14) that separates from the first amacrine cell cluster.
source: Additionally, there is a second cluster of amacrine cells (cluster 14) that separates from the first amacrine cell cluster.
evidence: This cluster identification is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells progressed over time from left to right on the UMAP, from the uninjured, to the 44 hpl, the 4 dpl, as well as the 6 dpl enriched samples.
source: Similar to the progression of cellular identities, cells progressed over time from left to right, from the uninjured, to the 44 hpl, the 4 dpl, as well as the 6 dpl enriched samples.
evidence: This temporal progression is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells belonging to non-reactive MG were found at all sampled time points.
source: As expected, cells belonging to non-reactive MG were found at all sampled time points.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The vast majority of cells of the uninjured sample belonged to cluster 1 as well as cluster 2.
source: In particular, the vast majority of cells of the uninjured sample belonged to cluster 1 as well as cluster 2.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: A small proportion of cells in the uninjured sample aligned in a trajectory from non-reactive MG (left side of the map) through reactive MG (middle part) to RPCs and differentiating progeny (right side).
source: However, we also observed a small proportion of cells (Figure 2B) aligning in a trajectory from non-reactive MG (left side of the map) through reactive MG (middle part) to RPCs and differentiating progeny (right side) in the uninjured sample.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 44 hpl, cells mapping to non-reactive MG were still abundantly present, although mostly shifted right towards a cluster representing reactive MG (cluster 3).
source: At 44 hpl, cells mapping to non-reactive MG were still abundantly present, although mostly shifted right towards a cluster representing reactive MG (cluster 3).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells belonging to the cluster of reactive MG (cluster 3) were highly enriched at 44 hpl.
source: Cells belonging to this cluster of reactive MG were also highly enriched in this sample.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells mapping to the second cluster of reactive MG (cluster 4) as well as to RPCs (clusters 5–9) were overrepresented at 4 dpl, in line with the reported peak in proliferation at this time point.
source: In contrast, cells mapping to the second cluster of reactive MG (cluster 4) as well as to RPCs (clusters 5–9) were overrepresented at 4 dpl, in line with the reported peak in proliferation at this time point (Bernardos et al., 2007; Fausett and Goldman, 2006).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citations and figure reference.

claim: Cells mapping to RPCs were still frequently present at 6 dpl.
source: Cells mapping to RPCs were still frequently present at 6 dpl.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells belonging to regenerated progeny (clusters 10–15), which first appear at 4 dpl, became predominantly enriched at 6 dpl.
source: Moreover, cells belonging to regenerated progeny (clusters 10–15), which first appear at 4 dpl, became predominantly enriched at 6 dpl.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells mapping to reactive MG of the second cluster (cluster 4) and the abutting portion of non-reactive MG (cluster 1) were also enriched at 6 dpl, indicating a reversed direction.
source: In addition to the overall progression from left to right, we noted that cells mapping to reactive MG of the second cluster (cluster 4) and the abutting portion of non-reactive MG (cluster 1) were also enriched at this time point, indicating a reversed direction.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Most cells of the left side and lower middle part as well as cells branching from the right side of the map were in G1, which comprised most non-reactive MG (clusters 1 and 2), one cluster of reactive MG (cluster 4), one RPC population (cluster 7) and the regenerated progeny (clusters 10–15).
source: Consistently, we observed that most cells of the left side and lower middle part as well as cells branching from the right side of the map were in G1, which comprised most non-reactive MG (clusters 1 and 2), one cluster of reactive MG (cluster 4), one RPC population (cluster 7) and the regenerated progeny (clusters 10–15).
evidence: This cell cycle analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells in S phase were enriched in two domains of the middle part corresponding to reactive MG (cluster 3) and RPCs (clusters 5 and 7).
source: Cells in S phase were also present on the left side of the map, which represent non-reactive MG (clusters 1 and 2), but were in particular enriched in two domains of the middle part corresponding to reactive MG (cluster 3) and RPCs (clusters 5 and 7).
evidence: This cell cycle analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Two domains on the right side of the map showed an accumulation of cells in S phase, which include photoreceptor and horizontal cell precursors (clusters 8 and 9).
source: In addition, two domains on the right side of the map showed an accumulation of cells in S phase, which include photoreceptor and horizontal cell precursors (clusters 8 and 9).
evidence: This cell cycle analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: High pcna expression was observed in one population of reactive MG (cluster 3) and in RPCs (clusters 5, 6, 8, and 9).
source: When plotting pcna expression onto the main UMAP of the single cell transcriptome, we observed high counts in one population of reactive MG (cluster 3) and in RPCs (clusters 5, 6, 8, and 9).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Clusters 1 and 2 express apoeb, glula, cahz, rlbp1a as marker genes.
source: In our scRNAseq dataset, we found clusters 1 and 2 expressing apoeb, glula, cahz, rlbp1a as marker genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: High apoeb expression was observed in clusters 1 and 2, as well as in clusters 3 and 4.
source: When plotting apoeb expression onto the UMAP, we observed high counts in clusters 1 and 2, as well as in clusters 3 and 4 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The glial marker gfap showed high counts in clusters 1–4 and displayed high counts in cluster 5 as well.
source: The glial marker gfap, found among the top 100 upregulated marker genes for cluster 4 (Supplementary file 1), showed a similar pattern, with high counts in clusters 1–4, but displayed high counts in cluster 5 as well (Figure 3A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: Clusters 1–4 were identified as MG populations based on the expression pattern of apoeb and gfap.
source: Given the expression pattern of apoeb and gfap, we identified clusters 1–4 as MG populations.
evidence: This cluster annotation is based on marker gene expression.

claim: Clusters 1 and 2 were identified as non-reactive MG and clusters 3 and 4 as reactive MG.
source: Further analysis indicated clusters 1 and 2 as non-reactive MG and clusters 3 and 4 as reactive MG (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Non-reactive MG, which were mostly in G1 and did not express any injury-specific markers, showed counts for mstnb.
source: Non-reactive MG, which were mostly in G1 and did not express any injury-specific markers (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) showed counts for mstnb (Figure 3B).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Members of the retinoic acid signalling pathway, like rdh10a, aldh1a3, dhrs3a were enriched in non-reactive MG clusters.
source: In addition, members of the retinoic acid signalling pathway, like rdh10a, aldh1a3, dhrs3a (D'Aniello et al., 2015; Feng et al., 2010; Holmes and Hempel, 2011) were enriched in these clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This pathway enrichment is stated and supported by citations, figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: The UMAP plot of inhbaa showed strong expression only in clusters 1, 3, and 4, but not in cluster 2.
source: For instance, the UMAP plot of inhbaa, an evolutionarily conserved vertebrate glia marker (Hoang et al., 2020) showed strong expression only in clusters 1, 3, and 4, but not in cluster 2 (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by citation, figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: Reactive MG downregulated some glial markers, like glula and rlbp1a, and upregulated inflammatory cytokines, like crlf1a, matrix metalloproteases, like mmp9, and growth factors like hbegfa in the regenerating retina.
source: Reactive MG on the other hand downregulated some glial markers, like glula and rlbp1a, and upregulated inflammatory cytokines, like crlf1a, matrix metalloproteases, like mmp9, and growth factors like hbegfa in the regenerating retina (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: High crlf1a counts were observed in clusters 3 and 4, as well as in cluster 5.
source: Consistent with that, plotting of crlf1a expression onto the UMAP showed high read counts in clusters 3 and 4, as well as in cluster 5 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Only cluster 3, but not cluster 4 expressed Hairy-related downstream targets of active Notch signalling including her15.1–1, her9, and her4.1.
source: Again, DEG analysis showed that reactive MG can be subdivided further, because only cluster 3, but not cluster 4 expressed Hairy-related downstream targets of active Notch signalling including her15.1–1, her9, and her4.1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: The UMAP plot of her4.1 showed strong expression in cluster 3 as well as in cluster 5.
source: Indeed, the UMAP plot of her4.1 showed strong expression in cluster 3 as well as in cluster 5 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: her4.1 signal was not present in the uninjured retina, but appeared at 44 hpl in the inner nuclear layer of the central retina.
source: In agreement with our scRNAseq dataset, her4.1 signal was not present in the uninjured retina, but appeared at 44 hpl in the inner nuclear layer of the central retina (Figure 3D).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 4 and 6 dpl, her4.1 transcripts remained in the inner nuclear layer and appeared in cells of the outer nuclear layer too.
source: At 4 and 6 dpl, her4.1 transcripts remained in the inner nuclear layer and appeared in cells of the outer nuclear layer too (Figure 3D).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: DEG analysis revealed starmaker (stm) as a highly specific marker for reactive MG in cluster 3, but not for reactive MG in cluster 4.
source: DEG analysis revealed starmaker (stm) as a highly specific marker for reactive MG in cluster 3, but not for reactive MG in cluster 4 (Supplementary files 1 and 3).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by supplementary file reference.

claim: stm expression was observed only at 44 hpl, but not detected in the uninjured as well as in the 4 and 6 dpl retinal samples.
source: In agreement with our scRNAseq results, we observed stm expression only at 44 hpl, but did not detect any stm expression in the uninjured as well as in the 4 and 6 dpl retinal samples (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Virtually all stm-positive cells at 44 hpl displayed a MG morphology and were positive for Zrf1 (detecting GFAP) as well as PCNA.
source: Virtually, all stm-positive cells at 44 hpl displayed a MG morphology (Figure 3—figure supplement 2, yellow arrowhead) and were positive for Zrf1 (detecting GFAP) as well as PCNA.
evidence: This immunohistochemistry result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: crlf1a was not detectable in the uninjured, central retina, but was upregulated in Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells at 44 hpl.
source: Consistent with our scRNAseq dataset, crlf1a was not detectable in the uninjured, central retina, but was upregulated in Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells at 44 hpl (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 4 dpl, crlf1a signal was still present in Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells and returned back to undetectable levels at 6 dpl.
source: At 4 dpl, crlf1a signal was still present in Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells and returned back to undetectable levels at 6 dpl (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity was observed in MG during regeneration, with two non-reactive and two reactive MG populations that express distinct marker genes.
source: Taken together, we observed cellular heterogeneity in MG during regeneration, and identified two non-reactive and two reactive MG populations that express distinct marker genes.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: Cluster 5 locates next to the reactive MG (clusters 3 and 4), is highly proliferative and only becomes eminent at 4 dpl.
source: As mentioned above, several MG-related genes, like gfap or crlf1a, were also expressed in cluster 5, which locates next to the reactive MG (clusters 3 and 4), is highly proliferative and only becomes eminent at 4 dpl.
evidence: This cluster characterization is stated.

claim: Cluster 5 expressed several members of the High Mobility Group (Hmg) protein family among the top 100 upregulated marker genes.
source: Further analysis of this cluster showed expression of several members of the High Mobility Group (Hmg) protein family among the top 100 upregulated marker genes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by supplementary file reference.

claim: Cells of cluster 5 might have hybrid characteristics of reactive MG and downstream RPCs.
source: This indicated a transition from MG to RPC fate in the course of regeneration and that cells of cluster 5 might have hybrid characteristics of reactive MG and downstream RPCs.
evidence: This interpretation is stated based on gene expression patterns.

claim: When compared to reactive MG, cells of cluster 5 showed expression of several genes, including stmn1a, nr2e1 and sox9b.
source: When compared to reactive MG, cells of cluster 5 showed expression of several genes, including stmn1a, nr2e1 and sox9b (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary files 4 and 5).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: UMAP expression profile of stmn1a showed counts prevalently in cluster 5 and neighbouring, downstream RPCs on the right side of the map, but not in the reactive or non-reactive MG on the left side.
source: Consistently, UMAP expression profile of stmn1a showed counts prevalently in cluster 5 and neighbouring, downstream RPCs on the right side of the map, but not in the reactive or non-reactive MG on the left side (Figure 5A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The UMAP profiles of sox9b and nr2e1 showed strong expression almost exclusively restricted to cluster 5.
source: The UMAP profiles of sox9b and nr2e1 showed strong expression almost exclusively restricted to cluster 5.
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: DEG analysis between cluster 5 and the neighbouring downstream cluster 6 revealed expression of nr2e1 and sox9b, but additionally transcripts like id1.
source: DEG analysis between cluster 5 and the neighbouring downstream cluster 6 revealed also expression of nr2e1 and sox9b, but additionally transcripts like id1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: High id1 counts were found in cluster 5 and in other reactive or non-reactive MG clusters, but not in downstream RPCs on the right side of the map.
source: Consistently, high id1 counts were found in cluster 5 and in other reactive or non-reactive MG clusters, but not in downstream RPCs on the right side of the map (Figure 5A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: hmgb2b signal was not detectable in the uninjured, central retina, but was initiated in individual cells residing in the inner nuclear layer at 44 hpl.
source: Consistent with our scRNAseq data, hmgb2b signal was not detectable in the uninjured, central retina, but was initiated in individual cells residing in the inner nuclear layer at 44 hpl (Figure 5B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: hmgb2b transcripts could be detected in clusters of cells in the inner and outer nuclear layers at 4 and 6 dpl.
source: Subsequently, hmgb2b transcripts could be detected in clusters of cells in the inner and outer nuclear layers at 4 and 6 dpl (Figure 5B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: id1 expression was already detectable in Zrf1-positive but PCNA-negative cells in the inner nuclear layer of the uninjured, central retina.
source: Expression of id1 was already detectable in Zrf1-positive but PCNA-negative cells in the inner nuclear layer of the uninjured, central retina (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 44 hpl, id1 was strongly upregulated and co-localized with Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells in the inner nuclear layer.
source: At 44 hpl, id1 was strongly upregulated and co-localized with Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells in the inner nuclear layer.
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 4 and 6 dpl, id1 expression was still associated with Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells and, occasionally, with PCNA-only positive cells.
source: At 4 and 6 dpl, id1 expression was still associated with Zrf1/PCNA-double positive cells and, occasionally, with PCNA-only positive cells (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells in cluster 5 display a transcriptional signature of reactive MG, as well as RPCs, which is why it was assigned a hybrid identity.
source: In summary, marker analysis reveals that cells in cluster 5 display a transcriptional signature of reactive MG, as well as RPCs, which is why we assigned it a hybrid identity.
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated based on marker analysis.

claim: Cluster 6 upregulated insm1a, which has been described to promote cell cycle exit of RPCs in the injured fish retina at 4 dpl.
source: The before-mentioned DEG-analysis between cluster 5 (hybrid cells) and cluster 6 (neighbouring, downstream RPCs) also revealed that the latter upregulated insm1a (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and Supplementary file 6), which has been described to promote cell cycle exit of RPCs in the injured fish retina at 4 dpl (Ramachandran et al., 2012).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by citation, figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: DEG analysis showed upregulation of atoh7 and onecut2 in cluster 6.
source: In addition, our DEG analysis showed upregulation of atoh7 and onecut2 in cluster 6 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This differential gene expression is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: The highly redundant gene onecut1 was also expressed in cluster 6, albeit this was not found in the DEG analysis.
source: We found that the highly redundant gene onecut1 was also expressed in cluster 6, albeit this was not found in the DEG analysis.
evidence: This gene expression observation is stated.

claim: The UMAP expression profile of insm1a confirmed high read counts in cluster 6 but also in clusters 7, 8, and 10.
source: As expected, the UMAP expression profile of insm1a confirmed high read counts in cluster 6 but also in clusters 7, 8, and 10 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The UMAP expression profile of atoh7 confirmed expression in cluster 6, as well as in clusters 7 and 10.
source: The UMAP expression profile of atoh7 also confirmed expression in cluster 6, as well as in clusters 7 and 10 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The UMAP expression profile of onecut1 and onecut2 confirmed that both genes were expressed in clusters 6 and 7 and in addition in cluster 9.
source: Moreover, the UMAP expression profile of onecut1 and onecut2 confirmed that both genes were expressed in clusters 6 and 7 and in addition in cluster 9 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cluster 7 expressed additional neurogenic marker genes like tubb5 and sox11b.
source: Cluster 7 expressed additional neurogenic marker genes like tubb5 and sox11b (Baraban et al., 2013; Lange et al., 2020; Mu et al., 2017; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by citations, figure and supplementary file reference.

claim: The cell cycle status and the UMAP expression of mki67 showed read counts in cluster 6, but not in cluster 7.
source: Finally, the cell cycle status and the UMAP expression of mki67, a mitotic marker, showed read counts in cluster 6, but not in cluster 7 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cluster 6 and cluster 7 represented neurogenic progenitors, and were named progenitors 2 and progenitors 3, respectively.
source: Hence, we concluded that cluster 6 and cluster 7 represented neurogenic progenitors, and were named progenitors 2 and progenitors 3, respectively.
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated based on marker analysis.

claim: atoh7 signal was absent in the uninjured and 44 hpl retina, but became detectable in the inner and outer nuclear layers at 4 and 6 dpl.
source: In agreement with our scRNAseq data, atoh7 signal was absent in the uninjured and 44 hpl retina, but became detectable in the inner and outer nuclear layers at 4 and 6 dpl (Figure 7B).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: onecut1 and onecut2 were prominently expressed in the inner and outer nuclear layer at 4 and 6 dpl, in addition to their homeostatic expression in the presumptive horizontal cell layer in the uninjured and 44 hpl retina.
source: Similarly, onecut1 and onecut2 were prominently expressed in the inner and outer nuclear layer at 4 and 6 dpl, in addition to their homeostatic expression in the presumptive horizontal cell layer in the uninjured and 44 hpl retina (Figure 7B, black arrowheads).
evidence: This in situ hybridization result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: scRNAseq showed heterogeneity of neurogenic progenitors, which upregulate known markers of retinogenesis in the regenerating retina.
source: In summary, scRNAseq showed heterogeneity of neurogenic progenitors, which upregulate known markers of retinogenesis in the regenerating retina.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: Gene expression analysis of cluster 8 showed significant upregulation of several well-known photoreceptor precursor markers, including crx, and thrb.
source: Gene expression analysis of cluster 8, which locates next to the neurogenic progenitors (cluster 6 and 7), showed significant upregulation of several well-known photoreceptor precursor markers, including crx, and thrb (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by supplementary file reference.

claim: UMAP plots for crx and thrb revealed high counts in cluster 8.
source: Consistently, UMAP plots for crx and thrb revealed high counts in cluster 8 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Clusters 11 and 12 represent differentiating photoreceptors giving rise to blue and red cones as shown by the UMAP plots of opn1sw2 and opn1lw2, respectively.
source: Precisely, clusters 11 and 12 represent differentiating photoreceptors giving rise to blue and red cones as shown by the UMAP plots of opn1sw2 and opn1lw2, respectively (Figure 8B).
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cluster 9 expressed known developmental markers of horizontal cell precursors like prox1a and rem1.
source: Cluster 9, which abuts the neurogenic progenitor 3 (cluster 7), expressed known developmental markers of horizontal cell precursors like prox1a and rem1 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by supplementary file reference.

claim: The UMAP plot for rem1 showed high expression almost restricted to cluster 9 specifically.
source: Consistently, the UMAP plot for rem1 showed high expression almost restricted to this cluster specifically.
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Gene expression analysis revealed ptf1a expression in cluster 9, which has been shown to be required for lineage specification of horizontal and amacrine cells in the developing retina.
source: Gene expression analysis also revealed ptf1a expression in cluster 9, which has been shown to be required for lineage specification of horizontal and amacrine cells in the developing retina (Jusuf et al., 2011; Jusuf and Harris, 2009).
evidence: This marker gene expression is stated and supported by citations.

claim: The UMAP expression profile of ptf1a confirms high counts in the left part of cluster 9, but is even more pronounced in the upstream part of cluster 7 feeding into cluster 9.
source: In line with these findings, the UMAP expression profile of ptf1a confirms high counts in the left part of cluster 9, but is even more pronounced in the upstream part of cluster 7 feeding into cluster 9 (Figure 8C).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Gene expression analysis of clusters 10, 13, 14, and 15 identified them as differentiating progeny giving rise to retinal ganglion cells (cluster 10), amacrine cells (clusters 13 and 14), as well as bipolar cells (cluster 15), respectively.
source: Gene expression analysis of the remaining clusters 10, 13, 14, and 15 identified them as differentiating progeny giving rise to retinal ganglion cells (cluster 10), amacrine cells (clusters 13 and 14), as well as bipolar cells (cluster 15), respectively (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated and supported by supplementary file reference.

claim: UMAP plots of gap43 and the more mature retinal ganglion cell marker isl2b showed a strong upregulation in cluster 10.
source: In this context, UMAP plots of gap43 and the more mature retinal ganglion cell marker isl2b showed a strong upregulation in cluster 10 (Figure 8D).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: UMAP plots of stx1b and pvalb6, markers of differentiating and mature amacrine cells, revealed strong expression in clusters 13 and 14.
source: UMAP plots of stx1b and pvalb6, markers of differentiating and mature amacrine cells, revealed strong expression in clusters 13 and 14, whereas UMAP plots of vsx1 and samsn1a, known and novel markers of bipolar cells, respectively, showed high counts in cluster 15 (Figure 8E and F).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: UMAP plots of vsx1 and samsn1a, known and novel markers of bipolar cells, respectively, showed high counts in cluster 15.
source: UMAP plots of stx1b and pvalb6, markers of differentiating and mature amacrine cells, revealed strong expression in clusters 13 and 14, whereas UMAP plots of vsx1 and samsn1a, known and novel markers of bipolar cells, respectively, showed high counts in cluster 15 (Figure 8E and F).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The earliest committed progeny emerged at 4 dpl giving rise to retinal ganglion cells or to photoreceptors, in particular red cones.
source: We found that the earliest committed progeny emerged at 4 dpl giving rise to retinal ganglion cells or to photoreceptors, in particular red cones.
evidence: This temporal analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 6 dpl, the number of retinal ganglion cells and red cones continued to increase.
source: At 6 dpl, the number of retinal ganglion cells and red cones continued to increase.
evidence: This temporal analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: A significant number of blue cones and amacrine cells, as well as a small number of bipolar cells were detected at 6 dpl.
source: In addition, we detected a significant number of blue cones and amacrine cells, as well as a small number of bipolar cells at this time point.
evidence: This temporal analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: No differentiating progeny giving rise to horizontal cells or rods were detected at 6 dpl.
source: We did not detect any differentiating progeny giving rise to horizontal cells or rods at this stage.
evidence: This observation is stated.

claim: Expression of rho and gnat1, two markers of rod photoreceptors, was very low and sparse, and did not define any specific rod cluster.
source: Expression of rho and gnat1, two markers of rod photoreceptors, was very low and sparse, and did not define any specific rod cluster (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Expression of gad1b, which encodes for glutamate decarboxylase synthetizing the neurotransmitter GABA, was mostly restricted to amacrine cells (clusters 13 and 14).
source: Expression of gad1b, which encodes for glutamate decarboxylase synthetizing the neurotransmitter GABA, was mostly restricted to amacrine cells (clusters 13 and 14) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: High counts of chata were specifically found in amacrine cells (clusters 13 and 14), with chata expression detected only in cells located at the tip of cluster 13 and in all cells of cluster 14.
source: As expected, high counts of chata were specifically found in amacrine cells (clusters 13 and 14). In particular, chata expression was detected only in cells located at the tip of cluster 13 and in all cells of cluster 14.
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: calb2a was expressed in some reactive MG (cluster 3) and quite strongly in some amacrine cells (cluster 13).
source: calb2a was expressed in some reactive MG (cluster 3) and quite strongly in some amacrine cells (cluster 13).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: calb2a and calb2b were not detected in horizontal cell precursors (cluster 9).
source: Importantly, we did not detect any calb2a and calb2b in horizontal cell precursors (cluster 9).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: prkcab and prkcbb were not detected in bipolar cells.
source: Importantly, we did not detect prkcab or prkcbb in our bipolar cells.
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: High counts of snap25a were found in retinal ganglion and amacrine cells (clusters 10, 13, and 14).
source: Specifically, high counts of snap25a were found in retinal ganglion and amacrine cells (clusters 10, 13, and 14).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: High counts of snap25b were observed in retinal ganglion and amacrine cells (clusters 10, 13, and 14) as well as in red and blue cones (clusters 11 and 12) and the right part of the horizontal cell precursors (cluster 9).
source: High counts of snap25b were observed in the same clusters as well as in red and blue cones (clusters 11 and 12) and the right part of the horizontal cell precursors (cluster 9).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The scRNAseq data reveal the presence of fate-restricted progenitors and the sequential appearance of differentiating progeny in the light-lesioned, adult zebrafish retina.
source: Taken together, our scRNAseq data reveal the presence of fate-restricted progenitors and the sequential appearance of differentiating progeny in the light-lesioned, adult zebrafish retina.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: The analysis of more mature markers shows that the differentiation of retinal ganglion cells and red cones is preceding the appearance of blue cones, amacrine and bipolar cells.
source: Moreover, the analysis of more mature markers shows that the differentiation of retinal ganglion cells and red cones is preceding the appearance of blue cones, amacrine and bipolar cells.
evidence: This temporal sequence is stated based on marker analysis.

claim: The cluster annotated as resting MG in Hoang et al. mapped to clusters annotated as non-reactive MG 1 and 2 in the present dataset.
source: Consistently, the cluster annotated as resting MG in Hoang et al. mapped to clusters annotated as non-reactive MG 1 and 2 in our dataset (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The cluster annotated as activated MG in Hoang et al. mapped to clusters annotated as reactive MG 1 and 2, as well as to the cluster with hybrid identity of MG/progenitors in the present dataset.
source: The cluster annotated as activated MG in Hoang et al. mapped to clusters annotated as reactive MG 1 and 2, as well as to the cluster with hybrid identity of MG/progenitors in our dataset.
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Some cells annotated as activated MG in Hoang et al. mapped also to neurogenic progenitor 2 and 3 clusters in the present dataset.
source: Interestingly, some cells annotated as activated MG in Hoang et al. mapped also to neurogenic progenitor 2 and 3 clusters in our dataset (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The cluster annotated as progenitors in Hoang et al. mapped to the progenitor area in the present dataset, which included neurogenic progenitors 2, 3 as well as photoreceptor and horizontal cell precursors.
source: The cluster annotated as progenitors in Hoang et al. mapped to the progenitor area in our dataset, which included neurogenic progenitors 2, 3 as well as photoreceptor and horizontal cell precursors (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Retinal ganglion cells, cones, GABAergic amacrine cells and bipolar cells annotated in Hoang et al. perfectly mapped to retinal ganglion cells, cone, amacrine, and bipolar cells in the present dataset.
source: Finally, retinal ganglion cells, cones, GABAergic amacrine cells and bipolar cells annotated in Hoang et al. perfectly mapped to retinal ganglion cells, cone, amacrine, and bipolar cells in our dataset (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The horizontal cell cluster annotated by Hoang and colleagues mapped to reactive MG 2, MG/progenitors 1 and part of progenitors 3 in the present dataset.
source: While we did not detect a mature horizontal cell cluster, Hoang and colleagues annotated a horizontal cell cluster, which cells mapped to reactive MG 2, MG/progenitors 1 and part of progenitors 3 in our dataset (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Rod photoreceptors annotated by Hoang and colleagues mapped to progenitors 3, photoreceptor precursors, red and blue cones, horizontal cell precursors and bipolar cells in the present dataset.
source: Moreover, Hoang and colleagues annotated rod photoreceptors that mapped to progenitors 3, photoreceptor precursors, red and blue cones, horizontal cell precursors and bipolar cells in our dataset (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Hoang and colleagues annotated additional cell clusters that did not map to any cluster in the present dataset, and included oligodendrocytes, pericytes, retinal pigmented epithelial cells as well as vascular/endothelial cells.
source: Finally, Hoang and colleagues annotated additional cell clusters that did not map to any cluster in our dataset, and included oligodendrocytes, pericytes, retinal pigmented epithelial cells as well as vascular/endothelial cells (Figure 9B).
evidence: This comparison result is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The study is the first providing a comprehensive overview of MG, MG-derived cells and their lineage relationship up to 6 days post lesion in the zebrafish retina.
source: In contrast to these previous results, our study is the first providing a comprehensive overview of MG, MG-derived cells and their lineage relationship up to 6 days post lesion in the zebrafish retina.
evidence: This claim about the novelty of the study is stated.

claim: The selective enrichment of MG and their respective progeny allowed adequate single-cell resolution to observe substantial heterogeneity in the molecular identity of MG in homeostatic as well as regenerating conditions.
source: Due to our selective enrichment of MG and their respective progeny, we gain an adequate single-cell resolution to observe substantial heterogeneity in the molecular identity of MG in homeostatic as well as regenerating conditions.
evidence: This methodological advantage is stated.

claim: The study provides an in depth description of MG as well as RPC molecular identity, cell fate decisions and production of regenerated progeny that cover all key aspects during zebrafish retina regeneration.
source: We also provide an in depth description of MG as well as RPC molecular identity, cell fate decisions and production of regenerated progeny that cover all key aspects during zebrafish retina regeneration.
evidence: This claim about the comprehensiveness of the study is stated.

claim: Two main trajectories were defined in the regenerating zebrafish retina: a glial trajectory (clusters 1–5) that maintains the MG pool and generates first-born neurogenic RPCs, and a neurogenic trajectory (clusters 6–15) that gives rise to all retinal neurons.
source: Our strategy allowed us to define two main trajectories in the regenerating zebrafish retina (Figure 10). The first trajectory (solid and dashed red lines) comprises clusters 1–5 and constitutes a closed cycle that both maintains the MG pool and generates the first-born neurogenic RPCs. The second trajectory (solid black lines) involves clusters 6–15 and gives rise to all retinal neurons via the progressive restriction in cell fate competence of neurogenic RPCs.
evidence: This model is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: MG in the homeostatic zebrafish retina behave like multipotent RPCs.
source: In summary, MG in the homeostatic zebrafish retina behave like multipotent RPCs.
evidence: This summary statement is based on the observations.

claim: Upon injury, reactive MG express genes associated with inflammation, like crlf1a, and undergo asymmetric cell division.
source: Upon injury, reactive MG express genes associated with inflammation, like crlf1a, and undergo asymmetric cell division.
evidence: This summary statement is based on the observations.

claim: Cells in cluster 5, which displays a transcriptional hybrid identity between MG and RPCs, are the product of the asymmetric cell division from the early reactive MG (cluster 3).
source: Thus, we suggest that cells in cluster 5, which displays a transcriptional hybrid identity between MG and RPCs, are the product of the asymmetric cell division from the early reactive MG (cluster 3).
evidence: This interpretation is stated.

claim: Cells in cluster 5 represent a crossroad of the glial and neurogenic trajectory, containing self-renewed MG as well as first-born, MG-derived RPCs as a direct result of the earlier (44 hpl) asymmetric MG cell division.
source: Hence, we propose that cells in cluster 5 represent a crossroad of the glial and neurogenic trajectory, containing self-renewed MG as well as first-born, MG-derived RPCs as a direct result of the earlier (44 hpl) asymmetric MG cell division.
evidence: This model is proposed based on the data.

claim: Self-renewed MG close the cycle via late reactive MG (cluster 4), which is evident at 4 dpl, and return into non-reactive MG (clusters 1 and 2).
source: We further propose that self-renewed MG close the cycle via late reactive MG (cluster 4), which is evident at 4 dpl, and return into non-reactive MG (clusters 1 and 2, red, dashed line in Figure 10).
evidence: This model is proposed based on the data and supported by figure reference.

claim: Neurogenic RPCs map to the right of cluster 5, and include proliferating, neurogenic RPCs (cluster 6) and the downstream, non-proliferating, neurogenic RPCs (cluster 7).
source: Neurogenic RPCs map to the right of cluster 5, and include proliferating, neurogenic RPCs (cluster 6) and the downstream, non-proliferating, neurogenic RPCs (cluster 7).
evidence: This cluster characterization is stated.

claim: Cluster 6 and 7 are the roots of the neurogenic trajectory from which fate-restricted RPCs and regenerated progeny arise at 4 and 6 dpl.
source: We propose that cluster 6 and 7 are the roots of the neurogenic trajectory from which fate-restricted RPCs and regenerated progeny arise at 4 and 6 dpl (solid, black line in Figure 10).
evidence: This model is proposed based on the data and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cluster 10 represents differentiating retinal ganglion cells that are the first regenerated progeny, evident as early as 4 dpl.
source: Cluster 10 represents differentiating retinal ganglion cells that are the first regenerated progeny, evident as early as 4 dpl (Figures 7 and 10 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: Cluster 14 includes GABAergic amacrine cells, as shown by the expression of gad1b, which encodes for the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67.
source: In this respect, cluster 14 includes GABAergic amacrine cells, as shown by the expression of gad1b, which encodes for the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67 (Bosma et al., 1999).
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated and supported by citation.

claim: Cluster 15 includes a class of amacrine cells known as starburst amacrine cells, as indicated by the expression of both gad1b and chata.
source: In contrast, cluster 15 includes a class of amacrine cells known as starburst amacrine cells, as indicated by the expression of both gad1b and chata (O'Malley et al., 1992).
evidence: This cluster annotation is stated and supported by citation.

claim: Fate restricted precursors for regenerated cones and for horizontal cells are identified, as it occurs during development.
source: While amacrine cells arise directly from the core of neurogenic RPCs, fate restricted precursors for regenerated cones and for horizontal cells are identified (Figures 8 and 10), as it occurs during development (Godinho et al., 2007; Weber et al., 2014).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by citations and figure references.

claim: Red cones (cluster 11) branch from thrb-positive cells of the photoreceptor RPC cluster (cluster 8), consistently with the events during development.
source: Consistently with the events during development, red cones (cluster 11) branch from thrb-positive cells of the photoreceptor RPC cluster (cluster 8).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: thrb transcripts are found in neurogenic RPCs of cluster 7 as well as at the beginning of cluster 9, which contains horizontal cell precursors becoming evident at 4 dpl.
source: Interestingly, thrb transcripts are found in neurogenic RPCs of cluster 7 as well as at the beginning of cluster 9, which contains horizontal cell precursors becoming evident at 4 dpl (Figure 8B).
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Horizontal and cone cells share a common Thrb-positive progenitor in the developing zebrafish retina.
source: This is in agreement with observations in the developing zebrafish retina, where horizontal and cone cells share a common Thrb-positive progenitor (Suzuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This comparison to development is supported by a citation.

claim: Mature markers of horizontal cells, like calbindins, are not found in cluster 9.
source: Mature markers of horizontal cells, like calbindins, are not found in cluster 9 (Figure 8B, Figure 8—figure supplement 2C and Supplementary file 1), in contrast to cone photoreceptor mature markers, like red light- and blue light-sensitive opsins, at 4 and 6 dpl.
evidence: This gene expression analysis is stated and supported by figure and supplementary file references.

claim: The study is the first comprehensive description of the molecular network underlying MG self-renewal and RPC differentiation to regenerating neurons which will inform future regenerative therapies to treat retinal dystrophies in humans.
source: In summary, our study is the first comprehensive description of the molecular network underlying MG self-renewal and RPC differentiation to regenerating neurons which will inform future regenerative therapies to treat retinal dystrophies in humans.(Javed and Cayouette, 2017).
evidence: This claim about the significance of the study is stated and supported by a citation.
